ambiguities.text: The specification states monitoring continues if transaction 'not found in mempool' but doesn't clarify behavior if transaction hash is unknown and never appears
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume subscription remains active indefinitely until explicitly unsubscribed by client. Implementations should document this behavior.

ambiguities.text: No timeout or maximum subscription duration is specified for long-running subscriptions
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations may define their own resource limits. Clients should handle unexpected subscription termination.

ambiguities.text: The exact definition of 'finality' is not specified - could mean different things on different chains
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this refers to consensus-layer finality on PoS chains. On chains without finality guarantees, this notification may never be sent or may use a confirmation count threshold.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Ethereum node maintains a mempool and can track transaction propagation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Light clients or nodes without mempools may not be able to implement the full subscription behavior

implicit_assumptions.description: Users trust the node to accurately report transaction inclusion and reorg events
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious nodes could send false inclusion notifications, causing applications to act on unconfirmed transactions

implicit_assumptions.description: Applications using reorg monitoring will implement appropriate logic to handle notifications
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Applications that don't handle reorg notifications may have inconsistent state or double-spend vulnerabilities

implicit_assumptions.description: The notification mechanism provides transparency but does not prevent reorg-based attacks
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users may assume monitoring provides protection when it only provides visibility
